Axis PLM · Demonstration

VP2 BOM Walkthrough

One engineering change, taken end to end through the Structure Explorer — a part created, modified, revised, reviewed, released and removed. Every screen below is the running app, and every line of it is a read or write against MySQL.

Dataset
VP2 · D-Segment BEV
Items
26 lines
Database
MySQL 8.0.46
Tables
4
Stack
React · Express

The change

The cell module assembly CMA-21000 /A needs a temperature sensor it doesn't currently carry. An engineer adds the line, corrects the quantity and cost, revises it after a supplier conversation, raises a change request to get the new revision released, and finally removes the part again.

Nothing here is mocked in the browser. Each action is an HTTP call that runs in a transaction and writes a revision-history row and an activity-log row, so the same sequence is visible afterwards as an audit trail.

The sequence

11 steps
01

Start from the structure as released

GET /api/items

The product tree loads from the database at startup. CMA-21000 /A is selected: two child lines, find numbers 10.1 and 10.2, 21.1 kg rolled up.

02

Create the new line

POST /api/items

Every attribute the schema holds is editable on the way in. The part is placed at find number 10.3 under the selected assembly, bought from Nihon Cell Co., and starts life In Work with no effectivity date.

Recorded Created SNS-21300 /A — Module Temperature Sensor under CMA-21000
03

The line lands in its find-number position

GET /api/items · tree rebuilt

The new row appears in the tree and in the structure table between 10.2 and the next assembly — where a structure report would put it — and the selection moves to it.

04

Modify the quantity and cost

PATCH /api/items/:id

Four per module was wrong; it takes six, and the quoted cost came down. The revision is deliberately not editable here — revisions move only through the revise operation.

Recorded Modified SNS-21300 /A — Qty 4 → 6, Unit cost 11.25 → 9.8
05

Revise it to the next revision

POST /api/items/:id/revise

A tightened thermistor tolerance is a new revision, not an edit. Leaving the revision blank takes the next in sequence — /A → /B.

Recorded Revised SNS-21300 /A → /B — Thermistor tolerance tightened to ±0.5 K
06

The item carries its own history

GET /api/items/:id/history

Three actions, three rows, each tagged with the revision it was recorded against — which is what lets Compare Revisions show two distinct revisions rather than repeating the current one.

07

Raise a change request against it

POST /api/change-requests

A new revision needs approval to be released. The request is raised against the selected part and given an ECO number — ECO-4472.

Recorded Submitted ECO-4472 — Release SNS-21300 /B
08

Approve it, once

PATCH /api/change-requests/:id

The decision, the decider and the timestamp are all stored. A request that has already been decided cannot be decided again — the second attempt is refused rather than silently overwriting the first.

409 Change request is already approved
09

Search the items table

GET /api/items/search?q=…&state=…&mb=…

Search runs as SQL against items — part number, name, classification and supplier — narrowed by lifecycle state and make/buy. It finds the part created minutes earlier because it is querying the database, not a cached copy of the tree.

10

Structure rules are enforced in the database

DELETE /api/items/:id

Deletion is checked inside the transaction, not just hidden in the interface. An assembly that still has child lines is refused, and so is the top-level item — whose Delete button is disabled as well.

409 Item has 3 child line(s) — delete those first
409 The top-level item cannot be deleted
404 Unknown item "sns-21300"  — after deletion
11

Delete the line, keep the record

DELETE /api/items/:id

The part, its revision history and the change request raised against it are removed. Its activity rows are detached rather than deleted, so the log still shows what happened to a part that no longer exists — and the selection moves up to the parent assembly.

Recorded Deleted SNS-21300 /B — Module Temperature Sensor

The trail it leaves

activity_log

The Changes screen is the same sequence read back out of the database — every action, in order, with who did it and which part it touched.

The same run, scripted

npm run demo

The workflow above is also a command-line script, so it can be replayed without clicking through the interface. It cleans up after itself and can be run repeatedly.

npm run demo

What the demo touches

4 tables · 11 endpoints
Endpoint Operation Writes to
GET /api/itemsLoad the whole product structure—
GET /api/items/searchSearch by text, state, make/buy, kind—
POST /api/itemsCreate a part or sub-assemblyitems · revision_history · activity_log
PATCH /api/items/:idModify any editable attributeitems · revision_history · activity_log
POST /api/items/:id/reviseBump to the next revisionitems · revision_history · activity_log
DELETE /api/items/:idDelete a childless itemitems · revision_history · change_requests · activity_log
GET /api/items/:id/historyRevision history for one item—
POST /api/change-requestsRaise a request against an itemchange_requests · activity_log
PATCH /api/change-requests/:idApprove or reject, oncechange_requests · activity_log
GET /api/activityRead the audit trail back—
Captured from the running app on the claude/plm-structure-explorer-0jctb5 branch. Reset the dataset with npm run db:seed; replay the sequence with npm run demo. Setup instructions are in SETUP.md.
